response.basis: Extraction from numbered NL segments NL1-NL10 describing a train door/motion control state machine with DoorsClosing, InMotion (with substates Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching), Stopping, EmergencyStopping states.

contracts.basis: NL1: 'The system starts in the DoorsClosing state'

binding_hints.reason: The system is the enclosing owner of the initial edge.
DoorsClosing is the state entered by the initial edge.

contracts.normative_statement: The root/system must have an initial pseudostate edge entering DoorsClosing.
contracts.quote: The system starts in the DoorsClosing state
contracts.reason: NL1 explicitly states the system starts in DoorsClosing, establishing an initial-entry obligation at root scope.

binding_hints.reason: DoorsClosing is the stated origin of the transition.

contracts.normative_statement: DoorsClosing must transition to InMotion on the Closed/SendDeparted signal.
contracts.quote: transitions to InMotion when the doors are closed, triggered by the "Closed/SendDeparted" signal
contracts.reason: NL1 explicitly establishes the transition endpoint pair DoorsClosing->InMotion.

binding_hints.reason: InMotion is the shared source of the two alternatives.
Stopping is the destination of this alternative.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must transition to Stopping on arrival, indicated by the named signal.
contracts.quote: transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal
contracts.reason: NL2 explicitly establishes one alternative endpoint from InMotion to Stopping.

binding_hints.reason: InMotion is the shared source of the two alternatives.
EmergencyStopping is the destination of this alternative.
This is a data condition evaluated in addition to any event.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must transition to EmergencyStopping when an obstacle is detected.
contracts.quote: or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected
contracts.reason: NL2 establishes a second alternative endpoint from InMotion to EmergencyStopping under an obstacle-detected guard.

binding_hints.reason: Shared source of the disjoint alternatives.
One of the two alternatives requiring disjointness.

contracts.normative_statement: The two alternatives from InMotion (to Stopping and to EmergencyStopping) must be distinguishable/mutually exclusive.
contracts.quote: the system can either transition to the Stopping state ... or to the EmergencyStopping state
contracts.reason: NL2 uses 'either...or' to present two mutually exclusive alternative transitions from InMotion, establishing a disjointness obligation.

contracts.normative_statement: EmergencyStopping state must perform the Emergency Stop action.
contracts.quote: which includes the actions "Emergency Stop"
contracts.reason: NL3 explicitly requires the Emergency Stop action to be part of EmergencyStopping's behavior.

binding_hints.reason: State owning the required send action.
Named signal-send action required by NL.
The signal sent is itself an event concept.

contracts.normative_statement: EmergencyStopping state must send the Obstacle Detected signal.
contracts.quote: sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal
contracts.reason: NL3 explicitly requires sending the Obstacle Detected signal as part of EmergencyStopping's behavior.

binding_hints.reason: InMotion is the composite scope owning the substates.

cardinality_requirement.alternative_reading: explicit_named_members could also apply since the three names are explicitly listed.
cardinality_requirement.basis: NL4: 'the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching'
cardinality_requirement.reason: NL4 directly counts three named child states owned by the InMotion composite, representing motion phases, not concurrent regions.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must contain exactly three direct child substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching.
contracts.quote: the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching
contracts.reason: NL4 explicitly enumerates three named substates within InMotion, establishing a direct-child-state cardinality obligation.

contracts.normative_statement: Accelerating must be contained within InMotion.
contracts.quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating
contracts.reason: NL4 explicitly places Accelerating as a substate within InMotion.

contracts.normative_statement: Cruising must be contained within InMotion.
contracts.quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: ... Cruising
contracts.reason: NL4 explicitly places Cruising as a substate within InMotion.

contracts.normative_statement: Approaching must be contained within InMotion.
contracts.quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: ... and Approaching
contracts.reason: NL4 explicitly places Approaching as a substate within InMotion.

contracts.basis: NL5 text combined with prior discourse establishing InMotion as owner in NL4

binding_hints.reason: InMotion is the enclosing composite that owns the initial edge into its substates.
Accelerating is the substate entered by the initial edge.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must have an owner-local initial pseudostate edge entering Accelerating.
contracts.quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate
contracts.reason: Since NL4 established InMotion's substates, NL5's 'the system begins in Accelerating' is an owner-local initial-entry obligation of InMotion, not a root-to-Accelerating endpoint.

contracts.normative_statement: Accelerating must transition to Cruising on the Reached Cruising/Cruise signal.
contracts.quote: moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal
contracts.reason: NL5 explicitly establishes the transition endpoint pair Accelerating->Cruising.

binding_hints.reason: Data condition co-evaluated with the signal.

contracts.normative_statement: Accelerating must transition to Approaching upon the Approached/Decelerate signal when approaching the destination.
contracts.quote: it transitions to the Approaching substate upon receiving the "Approached/Decelerate" signal
contracts.reason: NL6 explicitly establishes a distinct transition endpoint pair Accelerating->Approaching, an alternative from Accelerating alongside NL5's Cruising target.

contracts.normative_statement: Cruising must transition to Approaching on the Approached/Decelerate signal.
contracts.quote: The system in the Cruising substate transitions to the Approaching substate when it approaches the destination, triggered by the "Approached/Decelerate" signal
contracts.reason: NL7 explicitly establishes the transition endpoint pair Cruising->Approaching.

binding_hints.reason: NL explicitly names Entry/Accelerate, giving an exact lifecycle phase.

contracts.normative_statement: Accelerating must perform the Accelerate action on entry.
contracts.quote: The system enters the Accelerating substate when motion begins, marked by the "Entry/Accelerate" action
contracts.reason: NL8 explicitly identifies an Entry/Accelerate action, supplying exact state, phase=entry, and action=Accelerate, making this S4-eligible.

binding_hints.reason: Named send action required by NL.
The signal sent is itself an event concept.

contracts.normative_statement: Approaching state must send the Send signal.
contracts.quote: the system sends the "Send" signal
contracts.reason: NL9 explicitly requires the Approaching state to send a named Send signal.

binding_hints.reason: Named continuous activity required by NL.

contracts.normative_statement: Approaching state must continuously perform the approach-destination activity while active.
contracts.quote: continues to approach the destination
contracts.reason: NL9 explicitly states the system continues to approach the destination, an explicitly continuous/repeated task independent from the discrete Send-signal action.

binding_hints.reason: Named exit condition bounding the retention obligation.

contracts.normative_statement: The system must retain Approaching as the active state while nearing the destination, until a stop/decelerate condition is ready.
contracts.quote: The system remains in the Approaching substate while nearing the destination, until it is ready to stop or decelerate
contracts.reason: NL10 explicitly establishes an obligation that the system stays in Approaching until a stop/decelerate readiness condition, an exact state-retention obligation without a supplied executable scenario.

candidates.expected: DoorsClosing, InMotion (and its substates Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching), Stopping, and EmergencyStopping must all be reachable from the root initial entry, since NL1 establishes DoorsClosing as the system start and the subsequent NL segments describe a continuous authored flow through these states.
candidates.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.reachability shows only llms_emp_feedback_final_0014 and UnspecifiedInitial reachable from [*]; every other declared state (DoorsClosing, InMotion, Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching, Stopping, EmergencyStopping, Entry, EmergencyStopping.UnspecifiedInitial) is marked reachable_from_initial=false and verify_facts reachability checks for all of them are status=refuted.
candidates.reason: This is the derived global reachability obligation implied by NL1's start-state framing; it is distinct from and does not replace the individual satisfied transition_endpoints contracts, which correctly describe existing edges that are simply unreachable due to the root initial-entry defect.
candidates.requirement_quote: The system starts in the DoorsClosing state and transitions to InMotion when the doors are closed
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: Each individual transition endpoint (DoorsClosing->InMotion, InMotion substates chain, InMotion->Stopping/EmergencyStopping) is present in the model, so one could argue local structural correctness suffices; but presence of an edge does not establish reachability when the sole root initial edge never enters the authored chain, so this is an independent global defect from the endpoint contracts.
candidates.title: Entire authored operating region unreachable from closed-model root

candidates.expected: The Entry/Accelerate action, carried on the InMotion default-entry edge into Accelerating, must be reachable and exercised as the state is entered.
candidates.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers for Entry_Accelerate lists consumer_transition_refs=['transition:line:15'] but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE diagnostic confirms the event has consumers but none is reachable from a top-level initial entry; verify_facts event-consumer check for Entry_Accelerate is status=refuted.
candidates.reason: The state_action obligation's exact carrier transition exists but its operational coverage is refuted; this is the behavioral consequence distinct from the pure declaration fact, so it is preserved as a W1 candidate on the same contract rather than silently satisfied.
candidates.requirement_quote: The system enters the Accelerating substate when motion begins, marked by the "Entry/Accelerate" action.
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The transition line 15 does exist and does carry the Entry_Accelerate trigger as its own local carrier, so the action-declaration itself is structurally present; the defect is that this exact carrier can never fire operationally because Accelerating (and InMotion) are unreachable from root, which is a consumer-coverage/reachability consequence rather than an absent action declaration.

cardinality_bindings.basis: NL4 quote 'Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching'; inspection_equivalent_facts.states shows InMotion (state:InMotion:line:11) with children Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching all parent=InMotion; exact_source_inventory states rows for InMotion.Accelerating/.Cruising/.Approaching parent=InMotion.
cardinality_bindings.reason: NL4 directly counts three named substates (Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching) owned by the InMotion composite as its direct children; this is a direct_child_states cardinality obligation on the InMotion owner, consistent across both lenses' contract-level scope rule. The owner is unreachable from root per the derived reachability contract, but that reachability defect is a separate property from the exact structural child-count obligation evaluated here.

result.reason: This lens audits root reachability, event-consumer coverage, initial-entry defects, and stable-termination consequences across the closed FCSTM. The closed model shows root [*] enters only UnspecifiedInitial (line 34), never DoorsClosing, so the entire authored graph (DoorsClosing, InMotion, its substates, Stopping, EmergencyStopping) is unreachable from root. This causes cascading violations: NL1-INIT-1's owner (root/system) initial edge exists but targets UnspecifiedInitial rather than DoorsClosing (wrong target, not merely a downstream reachability issue since the owner-local edge itself is malformed); all transition_endpoint contracts have their exact edges present in the inventory but are unreachable, which is a separate reachability property from endpoint existence (I preserve endpoint satisfaction and instead derive one narrow root-reachability contract); the initial edge at InMotion scope (line 15, [*]->Accelerating) carries a trigger despite being an unconditional pseudostate edge (INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL diagnostic), which is a genuine S2-decidable malformed nested initial-entry fact independent from root unreachability; event-consumer coverage is declared but not reachable for every event; and the EmergencyStopping.Entry/UnspecifiedInitial leaf states are compiler-owned/source-declared but unreachable so no independent deadlock claim is added since they are not established as required operating states beyond their own action/coverage obligations already covered by NL3 contracts.

decisions.basis: candidate, binding, and element_refs fields of dossier 0014:r3:i0 (state:llms_emp_feedback_final_0014:line:2, state:DoorsClosing:line:10, state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:9, transition:line:34).
decisions.reason: The exact closed-model fact is that the sole top-level initial edge (transition:line:34) targets the synthetic compiler-owned state UnspecifiedInitial (line 9), a distinct declared element from DoorsClosing (line 10), and UnspecifiedInitial has no outgoing transitions while DoorsClosing is marked unreachable from initial. The candidate's own strongest_rebuttal (that UnspecifiedInitial could be read as a labeling artifact for DoorsClosing) is explicitly excluded because the source/model identities are kept distinct and there is no edge from UnspecifiedInitial to DoorsClosing; this defeater is defeated by the exact distinct-element facts, leaving the initial-entry defect established.
decisions.violated_obligation: The root/system machine's initial pseudostate edge must enter DoorsClosing directly, per NL1 'The system starts in the DoorsClosing state'.

decisions.basis: candidate.observed and strongest_rebuttal fields of dossier 0014:r3:i10; element_refs for InMotion and its substates/transitions.
decisions.reason: The observed exact fact is that these events have declared consumer transitions but their reachable_consumer_transition_refs are empty. Per the property-preserving protocol, declared-but-unreachable consumer existence is a weaker property and does not rebut a contract requiring reachable consumers; the dossier's own strongest_rebuttal states this explicitly. No exact fact establishes reachable coverage, so the violation is established.
decisions.violated_obligation: Required events (Reached_Cruising_Cruise, Approached_Decelerate, Arrived_Stop_SendArrived, Obstacle_Detected) must have reachable consumers within the operating scope InMotion.

decisions.basis: candidate.observed, requirement_quote, and strongest_rebuttal fields of dossier 0014:r3:i11; element_refs state:EmergencyStopping:line:27, event:Obstacle_Detected:line:8.
decisions.reason: The exact source line 26 'EmergencyStopping : Obstacle Detected' is a PlantUML state-description string; the closed model has no action or transition attaching Obstacle_Detected to EmergencyStopping's lifecycle. decisions.violated_obligation: If EmergencyStopping must emit or be triggered by 'Obstacle Detected', it must appear as an action or transition label on EmergencyStopping, not merely a description.

decisions.basis: candidate, binding, and source_refs of obligation 0014:r3:i11 (0014.puml:line:26; llms_emp_feedback_final_0014.puml:line:25; event:Obstacle_Detected:line:8; state:EmergencyStopping:line:27)

The rebuttal that the model is self-consistent (the description is simply non-executable annotation reflecting the model author's own declaration) is a competent alternative supported by the exact PlantUML grammar and survives as a rebutting reading of design intent, though it does not erase the divergence from the NL contract requiring 'Emergency Stop' as an action.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The closed model is internally consistent with itself; the divergence is between the author's descriptive PlantUML text at line 26 ('EmergencyStopping : Obstacle Detected') and the declaration semantics that produced the model, so the model-side reading (that this is a mere annotation, not a missing action/trigger) is a reasonable design choice supported by the exact PlantUML syntax (':' introduces a description, not a transition or action).
